rules.law_name: Cartwright Act Common Pricing Algorithm Provisions
rules.citation: Business and Professions Code Sections 16729 and 16756.1
rules.title: Ban on certain uses or distribution of common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: A person may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement, trust, or conspiracy that restrains trade or commerce. A person also may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm to coerce another person to adopt a recommended price or commercial term for similar products or services in California.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to any “person” using or distributing a “common pricing algorithm” as defined by the statute; the text is not limited to housing.
coverage.summary: The statute broadly covers persons using or distributing common pricing algorithms in California, without stating housing-specific building or tenancy coverage.

rules.exemptions: “Person” does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.penalty: The Legislative Counsel’s Digest states that expanding the Cartwright Act expands activities whose violation is punishable as a crime, but the text does not state a specific penalty in this document.
rules.interaction: The statute states that nothing in this section impairs or limits the applicability of antitrust laws.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
